annotations.description: Choosing to go first in a 4-player multiplayer game is generally suboptimal. Going first means you draw fewer cards over the course of the early game compared to going later in turn order. In multiplayer, the advantage of playing first is diminished because you have three opponents rather than one, and the extra card from drawing is more valuable. Additionally, the hand has only one land (Forest) and will likely need to mulligan anyway, so going first with a weak hand provides no tempo advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose GLM47 Sarge (self) as starting player, going first in a 4-player game.
annotations.betterLine: In multiplayer, going last (or at least not first) is often preferred to maximize card draws and information. Choosing to go later in turn order would have been slightly better positioning.

annotations.description: Bottoming Warstorm Surge means the final 5-card hand will be Sol Ring + 4 lands with zero spells, entirely reliant on topdecking. Warstorm Surge is one of the best cards in a Vrondiss deck - each dragon token triggers 5 damage to any target. With Sol Ring, it could be cast as early as turn 3-4.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Warstorm Surge on the bottom of the library, keeping an all-mana hand with no action spells.
annotations.betterLine: Bottom a redundant land (like one of the two Forests or Mountains) instead, keeping Warstorm Surge + Sol Ring + 3 lands as a functional 5-card hand with a powerful payoff that synergizes with the commander.

annotations.description: Mosswort Bridge is a reasonable card to bottom in a vacuum, but in a Vrondiss deck that naturally creates 5/4 tokens, reaching 10 total power for Mosswort Bridge's activation is trivially easy. Mosswort Bridge lets you play a card for free, which is extremely powerful. One of the basic Forests or Mountains would have been a better bottom choice since the deck likely has plenty of basic lands, while Mosswort Bridge provides unique free-cast utility that synergizes perfectly with the commander's token generation.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Mosswort Bridge on the bottom of the library during mulligan/start-of-game card selection.
annotations.betterLine: Bottom a basic Forest or Mountain instead, keeping Mosswort Bridge for its powerful free-cast ability that is easy to activate in a Vrondiss deck with 5/4 tokens.

annotations.description: Playing Prosperous Innkeeper before playing the Barren Moor land is a sequencing error. With only 2 lands on the battlefield (Jungle Hollow and Tainted Wood), playing Barren Moor first would give 3 lands, then next turn they could have 4 mana available. By casting the Innkeeper first (using both lands), they miss the opportunity to play Barren Moor this turn since it should be played before spending mana. The Innkeeper creates a Treasure token which partially compensates, but playing the land first is strictly better sequencing - it doesn't change the ability to cast Innkeeper this turn (2 mana available either way) and ensures the land drop isn't missed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Prosperous Innkeeper without first playing Barren Moor
annotations.betterLine: Play Barren Moor first (tapped land, no mana cost), then cast Prosperous Innkeeper with the two untapped lands. This ensures the land drop is made and provides an extra land for future turns.

annotations.description: Declined to attack with Prosperous Innkeeper when no opponents had blockers available. While 1 damage is minimal in Commander, it was completely free with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with the 1/1 Prosperous Innkeeper.
annotations.betterLine: Attack one of the opponents (likely the one who seems most threatening or closest to a dangerous life threshold) with Prosperous Innkeeper for free 1 damage.

annotations.description: Passed the turn with exactly 4 mana available and Seer's Sundial in hand, the only castable spell. No instant-speed plays in hand to justify holding up mana. Every turn Seer's Sundial is delayed is a potential card draw missed from future land drops.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, wasting 4 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Seer's Sundial for 4 mana. It's the only playable card this turn, and deploying it early maximizes future landfall card draw triggers.

annotations.description: The player's reasoning says they want to cast Colossal Majesty (which costs {2}{G} and they have the mana for it with 2 Forests + Sol Ring), but they actually played Haven of the Spirit Dragon instead. Colossal Majesty is a key card draw engine, and while they have no creatures with power 4+ yet, casting it now sets up future card advantage once they deploy their commander Vrondiss (5/4). Playing Haven of the Spirit Dragon as the land drop is fine, but the player should have ALSO cast Colossal Majesty with their available mana (2 Forests + Sol Ring = 2G + 2C, more than enough for {2}{G}). Instead, it appears they only played the land and didn't cast Colossal Majesty despite having the mana and intending to do so based on their reasoning.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Haven of the Spirit Dragon as land drop but did not cast Colossal Majesty despite having the mana available (2 Forests untapped + Sol Ring).
annotations.betterLine: Play Haven of the Spirit Dragon AND cast Colossal Majesty using Forest + Sol Ring for the {2}{G} cost, setting up the card draw engine for future turns.

annotations.description: GLM47 Sarge has 4 lands in play (Jungle Hollow, Tainted Wood, Temple of Malady, and the Prosperous Innkeeper's Treasure token from entering). They have Exotic Orchard in hand and chose not to play it. With Exotic Orchard + existing lands, they could have 5 mana sources next turn. More importantly, they have Chatterfang (3 mana) available to cast this turn - they have 3 untapped lands (Tainted Wood, Temple of Malady, and one other) plus could play Exotic Orchard first. Wait - looking more carefully, the lands may be tapped from earlier plays. But the decision shows Chatterfang as a valid choice, meaning they have the mana to cast it. Playing Exotic Orchard first (it enters untapped since it's not a tapland) and then casting Chatterfang would be optimal - getting the 3/3 commander on board early with forestwalk and the token-doubling ability. Even if they can't cast Chatterfang this turn, they should at minimum play the Exotic Orchard to not miss a land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing Exotic Orchard or casting any spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Exotic Orchard (enters untapped), then cast Chatterfang, Squirrel General for {2}{G} using available mana. Getting the commander down on turn 5 starts generating value and applies pressure with forestwalk.

annotations.description: Failed to cast Colossal Majesty ({2}{G}) with available mana (Forest + Sol Ring). While they have no creatures with power 4+ yet, deploying this card advantage enchantment early ensures it's ready to trigger as soon as a large creature (like Vrondiss 5/4) hits the board. The mana was otherwise going to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Colossal Majesty for {2}{G} to set up future card draw, saving remaining mana for potential future plays.

annotations.description: With only 5 lands and no Sol Ring, casting Maskwood Nexus (4 mana) uses the entire turn but provides minimal immediate value - just making creatures all types. Chatterfang (3 mana) would leave mana open, provide a 3/3 body with forestwalk, and start generating squirrel tokens for future plays. Chatterfang also synergizes much better with the hand (The Odd Acorn Gang, Shamanic Revelation, End-Raze Forerunners) by building a board presence. Maskwood Nexus's creature type ability is largely irrelevant without a tribal payoff beyond Chatterfang's squirrel sacrifice ability, and its token-making ability costs 3 more mana. Chatterfang would have been the stronger play to start building board presence toward the powerful cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Maskwood Nexus for 4 mana, using all available mana for a minimal-impact artifact.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chatterfang, Squirrel General for 3 mana to start building board presence and generating squirrel tokens from Prosperous Innkeeper's treasure (which would also create a squirrel via Chatterfang). This advances the game plan toward Shamanic Revelation and End-Raze Forerunners much faster.

annotations.description: The player has an Island and a Plains in hand and has an untapped Plains and an untapped land available. They should play one of their land cards to avoid missing a land drop. They have mana available and Brainstorm in hand which could also be cast. Playing a land is free value and missing land drops in the early-to-mid game is a real cost, especially when holding cards like Mammoth Umbra (5 mana) that need more lands to cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing a land or casting Brainstorm, despite having both an Island and Plains in hand and not having played a land this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (or Plains) to make the 6th land drop, getting closer to casting Mammoth Umbra next turn. Could also cast Brainstorm with available mana to dig for more resources before playing the land.

annotations.description: Casting Anya before combat is suboptimal when the player has Lightning Greaves in hand and plans to equip it for haste anyway. However, the bigger sequencing issue is that the player should play their Mountain land drop first before casting spells, to have access to more mana and to potentially trigger Seer's Sundial (paying 2 to draw a card). With 5 lands + Seer's Sundial on board, playing Mountain first gives 6 lands and the option to pay 2 for a card draw. After playing Mountain (6 lands), they'd have enough mana to: play land (free) → potentially pay 2 for Sundial draw → cast Anya (5 mana) → cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana) → equip (0 mana), though that would require 9 mana total (2+5+2=9) and they'd only have 7 mana from 6 lands. Actually with 6 lands they have 6 mana, so they can cast Anya (5) and Lightning Greaves (2) = 7, which doesn't work. With 5 lands currently they have 5 mana available. Playing Mountain first gives 6 mana. They need 5 for Anya + 2 for Greaves = 7. Either way they can't cast both in one turn without more mana. But playing the land first before casting spells is still correct sequencing to maximize options and potentially trigger Seer's Sundial.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Anya, Merciless Angel before playing the Mountain from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first (triggering Seer's Sundial landfall, potentially paying 2 to draw a card if valuable), then cast Anya, Merciless Angel

annotations.description: Played a land before casting Brainstorm. With two excess Plains in hand, casting Brainstorm first would allow drawing 3 cards, putting back redundant Plains on top, and then making a more informed land drop. This is a classic Brainstorm sequencing mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains as land drop before casting Brainstorm
annotations.betterLine: Cast Brainstorm first (using the untapped Island), draw 3 cards, put back 2 (likely excess Plains), then play the best land from the resulting hand.

annotations.description: Casting Desolation Giant without kicker ({W}{W}) only destroys all OTHER creatures Kimi25 Analyst controls. Kimi25 Analyst has no other creatures on the battlefield - Lightning Greaves and Seer's Sundial are artifacts, not creatures. So the ETB trigger destroys nothing, making it just a vanilla 3/3 for 4 mana. Meanwhile, Kimi25 Analyst has board wipe potential with the kicked version (costs {2}{R}{R}{W}{W} = 6 mana) which would destroy all other creatures including GLM47 Sarge's Plaguecrafter and Prosperous Innkeeper. With only 4 untapped lands available, the kick isn't possible this turn, but deploying it without kicker wastes the powerful board wipe effect permanently. Faith's Fetters on Maskwood Nexus or Plaguecrafter would have been more impactful, neutralizing a key permanent while gaining 4 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Desolation Giant without kicker, getting a 3/3 body that destroys nothing (no other creatures controlled).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Faith's Fetters on a threatening permanent like GLM47 Sarge's Maskwood Nexus or Plaguecrafter, gaining 4 life and neutralizing a real threat. Save Desolation Giant for when you can kick it to wipe opponents' boards, or at least when opponents have more creatures to punish.

annotations.betterLine: Attack Gem25F Stoic with any single creature (even a 1/1 token) to eliminate them from the game.

annotations.description: Attacking the player at 51 life instead of the player at 30 life. With limited attack power, dealing damage to the higher-life player is less impactful. Attacking Kimi25 Analyst at 30 life would bring them closer to dangerous thresholds and is more strategically meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to attack GLM47 Sarge at 51 life
annotations.betterLine: Attack Kimi25 Analyst at 30 life, where the damage is proportionally more meaningful and brings them closer to half-life thresholds

annotations.description: Haiku Vorthos appears to have no creatures on the battlefield to enchant with Armored Ascension. The reasoning references 'Daxos' but no creature is present on their board. Casting an Aura with no valid target wastes the card and 4 mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to cast Armored Ascension with no creature on the battlefield to enchant.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Seachrome Coast or Plains) to develop mana, and wait to cast Armored Ascension until after deploying a creature (likely the commander) to enchant.

annotations.description: Seachrome Coast enters tapped since they control more than 2 other lands, providing no mana this turn. Plains would enter untapped and also increase the bonus from Armored Ascension in hand (+1/+1 per Plains). They already have blue mana from Island and Azorius Signet, making the blue from Seachrome Coast redundant.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Seachrome Coast, which enters tapped and doesn't count as a Plains.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains, which enters untapped for immediate use and increases Armored Ascension's bonus from +4/+4 to +5/+5 when eventually cast.

annotations.description: Failed to play a land before casting Warstorm Surge. They had Mountain, Blasted Landscape, and Command Tower in hand. Playing Command Tower first would give them an extra land on the battlefield for future turns at no cost. Additionally, at 13 life with no creatures to trigger Warstorm Surge immediately, Faith's Fetters (costing only 4 mana, gaining 4 life, and neutralizing a threat) might have been more defensively appropriate.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Warstorm Surge without first playing a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Command Tower first, then cast Warstorm Surge (or consider Faith's Fetters for the life gain and defensive utility given the low life total)

annotations.description: Haiku Vorthos chose to cast Armored Ascension before playing their Plains from hand. Since Armored Ascension gives +1/+1 per Plains controlled, playing the Plains first would have given an additional +1/+1 (5 Plains instead of 4). The land drop costs nothing and directly buffs the spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Armored Ascension with only 4 Plains on the battlefield, giving +4/+4
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains from hand first, then cast Armored Ascension to get +5/+5 instead of +4/+4

annotations.description: Kimi25 Analyst is at 6 life with no creatures to block and all lands tapped. GLM47 Sarge has The Odd Acorn Gang (5/5 menace/trample) plus multiple tokens on board. With Maskwood Nexus making everything Squirrels, they could use Squirrel tap abilities to pump The Odd Acorn Gang to 7/7+ and attack for lethal. Additionally, passing without playing Forest (land drop), Sol Ring, or Arcane Signet wastes significant mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the precombat main phase without casting any spells, playing lands, or using abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest, cast Sol Ring, cast Arcane Signet, use Squirrel tap abilities to pump The Odd Acorn Gang, then attack Kimi25 Analyst for lethal damage.
